details.description: Llama 3 70B Instruct is Meta's 70-billion-parameter instruction-tuned model from the original Llama 3 family, released April 18, 2024, and optimized for assistant-like chat. It is fine-tuned with supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), uses Grouped-Query Attention (GQA), and was trained on 15T+ tokens with a knowledge cutoff of December 2023. Meta's model card says Llama 3 instruction-tuned models "outperform many of the available open source chat models on common industry benchmarks," but this original Llama 3 has since been followed by Meta's longer-context Llama 3.1, 3.2, 3.3 and 4 releases.
advantages: Scores 82.0 on MMLU (5-shot), per Meta's model card.
Scores 81.7 pass@1 on HumanEval (0-shot), per Meta's model card.
Scores 93.0 on GSM-8K (8-shot, CoT), per Meta's model card.
Scores 50.4 on MATH (4-shot, CoT) and 39.5 on GPQA (0-shot), per Meta's model card.
Meta's model card directly compares this model to Llama 2 70B on the same benchmarks, reporting higher scores on every one (e.g. MMLU 82.0 vs. 52.9, HumanEval 81.7 vs. 25.6).
disadvantages: Meta's model card states Llama 3 is intended for commercial and research use in English only and was tested only in English.
Knowledge cutoff of December 2023, per Meta's model card.
Meta's model card does not describe tool-calling or function-calling support, unlike the later Llama 3.1, 3.2 and 3.3 releases.
Superseded by Meta's later Llama 3.1, 3.2, 3.3 and 4 releases, which extended the context window well beyond this model's 8K tokens, per those releases' model cards.
use_cases: Text extraction, classification, rewriting and summarization

notes: Catalog's 8,192-token max_input/max_output matches Meta's model card (8k context) and Fireworks' hosted page (8.2k) for this model. The Llama 3 model card doesn't itself describe tool-calling or the later releases' longer context; confirmed on the Llama 3.1 model card (128k context, tool-use benchmarks). The use_cases list is confirmed on Meta's Llama 3 launch blog post, which lists advice, brainstorming, classification, question answering, coding, extraction, rewriting and summarization as evaluated use cases; not stated verbatim on the model card itself.
